title: Attorney General of Texas

context.text: Incumbent Attorney General Ken Paxton is running for U.S. Senate, so the seat is open. Mayes Middleton and Nathan Johnson each won their May 2026 primary runoffs; Tom Oxford was selected at the Libertarian Party's April 2026 nominating convention.

candidates.name: Mayes Middleton
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 2026 Republican primary runoff.

summary.text: Mayes Middleton is the Republican nominee. A Galveston oil-and-gas executive and rancher, he served in the Texas House from 2019 to 2023 and has been a state senator since 2023, chairing the Freedom Caucus. He campaigns on supporting President Trump's immigration enforcement, creating a standalone election-integrity task force and an anti-corruption team, and continuing the office's conservative litigation; the Tribune reports he has put more than $17 million of his own money into the race.

background.text: President and CEO of Middleton Oil Company, a family business; also runs ranching, cattle and farming operations. Law degree and undergraduate degree from the University of Texas at Austin.
Texas House member 2019-2022 and Texas Senate member since 2023.
Described by The Texas Tribune as a longtime Republican donor.

priorities.text: Support President Trump's efforts to deport illegal immigrants, dismantle cartels and secure elections through dedicated divisions.
Root out corruption through an anti-corruption team, and create a standalone election-integrity task force with law-enforcement powers to prosecute election-related crimes.
Prevent "foreign adversaries" from buying Texas property, protect oil and gas jobs, and enforce transparency in how taxpayer dollars are used.
Pursue cases that defend Texas sovereignty, secure borders, election integrity and protect children, and combat fraud or abuse in government.

positions.summary: Says he would prioritize supporting President Trump's efforts to deport people in the country illegally and would enforce the president's border-security agenda.
positions.quote: Support Trump’s efforts to deport illegal immigrants, dismantle cartels and secure elections through dedicated divisions

positions.summary: Says he has led opposition to allowing men to compete in women's sports, among other policies.

record.text: The Texas Senate's press room lists an August 4, 2025 press conference by Middleton regarding Senate Bill 7, relating to the designation and use of certain spaces and facilities according to biological sex.
Served on the Senate Education K-16 and Jurisprudence committees (both dissolved September 4, 2025), per his official profile.

candidates.name: Nathan Johnson
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 2026 Democratic primary runoff.

summary.text: Nathan Johnson is the Democratic nominee. A Dallas attorney and mediator, he has been a state senator since 2019 and says he has passed 134 bills across water, energy, education, health care and criminal justice. He campaigns on investigating corruption in the public and private sectors, consumer protection and antitrust enforcement, partnering with district attorneys, and suing the federal government over what he calls unconstitutional border policy.

background.text: Bachelor's degree from the University of Arizona and law degree from the University of Texas; litigator and mediator with Thompson Coburn in Dallas.
Texas Senate member since 2019, first elected in 2018, representing part of Dallas County.

priorities.text: Rebuild the Attorney General's office, investigate and prosecute corruption in the public and private sectors, and revive consumer protection against fraud, AI scams and price fixing.
Enforce fair-competition laws to counter monopoly power and partner with district attorneys to improve public safety.
Enforce election laws without bias, investigating voter fraud, election-official intimidation and improper purging of voter rolls.

statements.quote: border policy and tactics that violate the U.S. Constitution
statements.context: Quoted by The Texas Tribune on the federal actions he says he would sue over

record.text: Filed a set of cannabis bills during the 2025 special session, announced July 30, 2025, including proposals to regulate hemp-derived THC products and to decriminalize adult-use cannabis.
Served as vice chair of the Senate Jurisprudence Committee and on the Business and Commerce and Transportation committees (Jurisprudence dissolved September 4, 2025), per his official profile.

candidates.name: Tom Oxford
candidates.ballotNote: Selected at the Texas Libertarian Party's April 2026 nominating convention.

summary.text: Tom Oxford is the Libertarian nominee, an attorney from Nederland who has practiced since 1982 in personal injury, immigration and civil rights. The Texas Tribune did not find public information about his policy stances, and he did not respond to Community Impact's questionnaire.

background.text: Owns Oxford Law PLLC in Jefferson County; graduated from the University of Texas and the University of Houston College of Law.
Has argued cases before the Texas Supreme Court and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit.

sources.title: 2026 Texas attorney general race: Who is running and what to know
Q&A: Get to know the candidates running for Texas attorney general

researchNotes: Slate: the Texas Secretary of State's candidate pages return 403 and no county sample ballot was loaded; the three-candidate slate rests on the Texas Tribune (Oct 5, 2026), Community Impact (Aug 31, 2026) and Ballotpedia, which agree; write-in candidates may also appear. Oxford has no campaign site or public statements found. Neither senator's floor votes were reviewed; record items are from their official Senate profiles. Middleton's and Johnson's other quotes in the Tribune were campaign-site paraphrases without verbatim text and are not used as positions. Texas's Secretary of State is appointed, so there is no SoS race.
